scope: Module 11 BlockEncoder match storage, key width, dictionary seeds and visit integration; fixed existing history horizon
mechanical_dependency: Root preserved the default parse_lazy wrapper with a narrow non-test dead_code allowance in src/match_parse.rs; encode now calls parse_lazy_with_budget.
api: BlockEncoder::search_retained_capacity() -> usize, all seven search vectors including inactive caches and ring
contracts: Both constructors preserve exact default dimensions; reset preserves selected search options.
SearchShape resolution precedes frame preparation and encode allocations; direct new().encode callers remain supported.

Selected dictionary seeds reshape through retained owners; working owners reshape only for changed layout or node count. No dictionary or a dictionary shorter than the selected width clears seeds without forced inactive reshaping.
Chain regular seed starts are D.saturating_sub(S+W-1)..=D-W when D>=W; small private range tests include S=1/2, and real seeds verify width-adjusted threshold positions.
Only dictionary content containing a complete regular key permits seed copying. Short dictionaries can still contribute complete boundary keys without copying stale-layout caches.

Greedy and Chain/Lazy use exact-width typed source keys, skip valid short tails and retain the minimum emitted match of four bytes. Concrete visits reach both Chain and Lazy current/lookahead selection.
Search retained capacity includes both Greedy vectors, both Chain head/node pairs and history. The wider codec capacity reuses that accounting once.
History remains bounded by the prior fixed128KiB horizon in this checkpoint. Configurable history and public Encoder controls are subsequent separate work items.
